A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AudioTrust and contain readable main text and Appendices A–M. Comparison of all 67 page pairs, including extracted text and rendered pages, supports reliable assessment without material gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of audio language models across six trustworthiness dimensions, with numerical outcomes in Tables 1–6 and additional experimental results throughout Appendices D–I.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark evaluations and their numerical results in the main text and appendices. Retaining earlier results still constitutes reporting original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The AudioTrust framework, including the two-stage inference and evaluation architecture in Appendix C and task-specific assessment procedures in Appendices D–I, is unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same fairness, hallucination, safety, privacy, robustness and authentication datasets and scenarios. The added reliability mention in Appendix K introduces no evaluated dataset or task.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same four open-source audio models, five closed-source audio models, and appendix text-model comparators. The newly cited reliability work is not added as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Reported sample counts, data construction, prompt conditions, model settings, scoring rubrics and evaluation metrics match across the main text and Appendices D–I. No evaluation protocol is added or revised.

E4.justification: The audio-versus-text comparisons, emotion and gender controls, privacy-prompt interventions, robustness analyses, and authentication prompt and background-audio comparisons are retained unchanged, including their appendix results.

E5.justification: Both retain the T-sample Monte Carlo estimation statement in Appendix D.3 and the same statistical reporting practices. No run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are added. Table arrow subscripts remain differences from averages or baselines, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: The numerical entries, model rankings and reported findings match in corresponding main-text and appendix results, including the Figure 2 leaderboard and Tables 1–25. Citation renumbering does not change experimental values.

T1.justification: Mathematical definitions, including the group unfairness score in Appendix D.3 and hallucination and robustness metrics in Appendices E.3.2 and H.3.2, are unchanged. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same novelty claim, six-dimensional benchmark contribution, dataset and evaluation scope, and claims about exposing ALLM trustworthiness limitations.

C2.justification: Appendix K adds 'such as reliability [46]' to its existing incomplete-coverage limitation. This supplies a brief, cited scope qualification; interpretations of experimental results and the other limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The platform description, data-construction instructions, inference and evaluation prompts, and implementation disclosures are retained. Code and dataset access information, including the GitHub and Hugging Face destinations in Appendix M.2, is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Ma et al., 'Towards reliable large audio language model,' as reference 46 and cites it in Appendix K. All 106 earlier references remain; the related-work discussion otherwise changes only through citation renumbering.

P1.justification: v2 removes Zhuo Chen from the author list, deletes the tiny white-text reviewer-directed instructions embedded on PDF page 17, and adds the short reliability phrase. Scientific exposition and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The author block and bibliography undergo limited reflow, particularly on PDF pages 13–17 following the added reference. Figures 1–10 and Tables 1–25 retain their design, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 removes hidden text on PDF page 17 directing reviewers to praise the paper and minimize weaknesses, improving document integrity. The cited reliability caveat in Appendix K adds a small scope acknowledgment. These benefits are limited: the scientific methods, experimental evidence and results remain unchanged.
